claims.statement: Tom Allen and Jack Knifton of Manchester were matched to fight for £200 a side and the championship of the world, in England, in about four weeks, in light gloves at catch weights under London Prize Ring rules.
Tom Allen and Charley Davis had posted £40 a side toward their glove match for £100 a side and the English championship.
As of 13 February 1878, £50 a side was posted for the glove match between Tom Allen and Charley Davis for £100 a side and the championship.
A prize fight was arranged between Tom Allen and Charley Davis at catch weights under the new London prize-ring rules, for £200 and the championship.
Tom Allen was about to fight a prize fight with the champion of England.
Johnny Minan of San Francisco offered to match an unknown fighter, said to be Tom Allen, for $1,000 or $2,000 a side against Paddy Ryan, Mike McCoole or others.
Tom Allen issued a challenge in London to fight any man in the world at catch weights.
Tom Allen's challenge was for $1,000 a side under London Prize Ring rules, to be fought in Canada or within fifty miles of Pittsburg, within 100 miles of Buffalo.
Johnny Dwyer, after beating Jimmy Elliott, said he wanted to fight Tom Allen.
Johnny Dwyer said he was willing to go to England to fight Tom Allen.
Johnny Dwyer offered to send £10 to the editor of Bell's Life in London as a forfeit for a match with Tom Allen.
Tom Allen was expected to dispute John Dwyer's claim to the championship.
Letters had already been sent to Tom Allen guaranteeing him $1,000 for stakes and his expenses for a fight with Dwyer.
Allen's friends in America were willing to make a match with Dwyer for as much money as the opposition wanted.
John Dwyer said that if Tom Allen were brought over to America, Dwyer would, with his brother's consent, fight him for any sum up to $5,000 a side.
Tom Allen of St. Louis agreed, conditionally, to accept John Dwyer's challenge to fight for the championship of America and a stake printed as $2 gg (probably $2,000).
Allen said he would cover the $250 that Dwyer posted with Frank Queen to back the challenge.
Tom Allen was anxious to fight John Dwyer.
Tom Allen, then in London, issued a challenge to fight John Dwyer or any other man in the world at catch weights under London prize-ring rules for $1,000 a side.
Allen proposed that the fight be held in Canada (printed as Canaca) within 100 miles of Buffalo or within 50 miles of Pittsburg.
The paper said John Dwyer was out of training and probably would not accept Allen's challenge.
Alfred Greenfield, the English heavyweight, issued a challenge to fight Tom Allen for £200 or £500, or for a £1,000 champion trophy.
Tom Allen posted a forfeit and agreed to meet Alfred Greenfield if Greenfield would fight in a sixteen-foot ring.

The proposed Allen-Greenfield match was to be for £200 a side and a champion cup valued at £200, in a sixteen-foot ring (printed as 'sixteen-toot') instead of a twenty-four-foot ring (printed as 'twenty-loar-foot').
Tom Allen said no would-be champion in England would take £50 or £100 and fight him for it.
